subject.title: fix(telegram): wire spooledUpdateHandlerTimeoutMs config to polling session

question: Should OpenClaw expose spooledUpdateHandlerTimeoutMs as a supported per-account Telegram configuration setting, rather than rely on and document the existing process-level environment override?
rationale: The patch adds a durable user-facing configuration and metadata contract; repository policy requires maintainer intent before expanding config surface when an existing override already controls the behavior.

options.title: Approve the account-level setting
options.body: Keep the new setting and document its per-account precedence over the existing environment fallback.

options.title: Keep environment-only control
options.body: Do not add the new config contract; instead document the existing environment override and its operational scope.

recommendation.title: Approve the account-level setting
recommendation.body: Keep the new setting and document its per-account precedence over the existing environment fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main Telegram ownership needs history verification before selecting a specific routing person.
